dimension-value-listed-twice.json.why: A value listed twice with different multipliers makes the rate depend on lookup order (6.3, M5).

entry-missing-source.json.why: Every entry needs a dated provider source so the pricing-auditor can verify it.

fee-token-multipliers-apply.json.why: Per-use fees are added after token cost and never multiplied (7.4), so token_multipliers_apply must be false.

negative-multiplier.json.why: A negative multiplier would make cost negative and let a ceiling fall below true cost (B1); decimals are unsigned.

no-base-rates-rule.json.why: An entry without a base_rates rule has nothing to fall back to outside the promotion window, so it is rejected rather than priced as zero.

rate-as-json-number.json.why: A rate written as the JSON number 0.5 would be parsed as a binary float, so money could lose exactness (6.4).

rate-with-exponent.json.why: Exact decimals are plain digits with an optional fraction; exponent notation such as 5e-1 is rejected so every consumer parses the same value.

rule-missing-source.json.why: Every rule needs its own dated source; a base_rates rule without one matches no rule type.

two-base-rates-rules.json.why: An entry with two base_rates rules is ambiguous about which rates apply, so exactly one is allowed.

unknown-rule-type.json.why: A rule type outside the seven in 6.3 has no defined place in the stacking order, so it matches no rule.
